chunks: 3217 - Muʿallā ibn Khunays narrated from al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام, who said:
I said to him concerning the saying of Allah, Mighty and Majestic,
"Indeed, Allah commands you to render trusts to their owners, and when you judge between people, to judge with justice."
He said: "It is upon the Imam to hand over what is with him to the Imam who comes after him. The Imams have been commanded to judge with justice, and the people have been commanded to follow them."

key_terms.الْأَئِمَّةُ: the Imams, who are commanded to rule and judge justly
key_terms.الْأَمَانَاتِ: the trusts, understood here as what is entrusted to the Imam and passed to its rightful holder
key_terms.الْإِمَامِ: the Imam, the divinely designated authority who bears and transfers the trust
key_terms.بِالْعَدْلِ: with justice, referring to judging fairly among people
key_terms.يَتَّبِعُوهُمْ: follow them, meaning the people are commanded to follow the Imams

ai.seo_question: How does Imam al-Ṣādiq عليه السلام interpret the verse about rendering trusts and judging with justice?
ai.summary: This hadith explains the verse as applying to the Imams عليهم السلام, especially regarding the transmission of the divinely entrusted authority from one Imam to the next. It also states that the Imams are commanded to judge with justice, while the people are commanded to follow them.
